scanner_doubts: navy_captain.md:616,626,633 - qe-math-002 is reported x6 and every one of the six is a next-period state, not a transpose. The sites are `\pi^{\prime}` at 616, 626 and 633 and `z^{\prime}` three times at 633, and 633 is the line that *defines* the prime: $\pi^{\prime}=\pi f_0(z^{\prime})/(\pi f_0(z^{\prime})+(1-\pi)f_1(z^{\prime}))$, the posterior after one more draw. The file contains no matrix or vector at all - no `bmatrix`, `pmatrix`, `\top` or `^T` anywhere - and $\pi$ is a scalar in $[0,1]$, so a transpose is not available in this lecture. In `tools/qestyle_rules.py` the first `lprime` branch is `(?:\\[A-Za-z]+|[A-Z]|\)|\}|\])(?:_\{[^}]*\}|_[A-Za-z0-9])?` + `PRIME_SUP`, which carries no juxtaposed-factor and no following-argument guard, so any `\command^{\prime}` counts and `\pi^{\prime}` matches there; `z^{\prime}` takes the lowercase branch, whose guard `(?!\s*(?:\(|\\left\s*\())` only excludes a following `(`, and here the prime is followed by `\right)`. Suggested narrowing: gate the `\prime` branches on the same `evident` juxtaposition test the two bare-apostrophe branches already use, or exempt a Greek-command base that carries no following factor. This is the difference between Math 4.5/10 and a high Math score for this file
